{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish at the start of the round and drew the whole plan on the scratch pad: three strokes, with the start at the nose, a split into top and bottom lines, and a rounded tail. The sketch gave every builder a clear job and a shape with a strong outline, and it is what the table built from. The finished fish stood as one connected run, and by our checks all 126 dominoes fell from the start.

Execution
I designed the sketch around what dominoes can do: gentle curves, lines leaving the nose in the same direction, and every stroke starting from a line already drawn. I then inspected the build closely at four points (2:00, 3:00, 3:30 and 4:15), covering the lower pinch, the tail joints and the closing of the loop. Each time I reported that the run was still connected, so the team always knew where it stood. Once the fish was complete, I asked everyone to take their hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration
I assigned the top line, bottom line and tail to Tom, Priya and Leo, so no one was left waiting. I kept the table updated through the build and answered Leo's concern about the tail pinch directly. I offered to take the lower curve and then focused on the joints at Leo's request, to avoid overlapping with the people already laying dominoes. I also asked Tom and Leo not to double up on inspections.

Leadership
I chose the animal, set the plan in the first minute and kept the table calm and on schedule. I made the call to stop building and protect the finished piece for the push. The table finished with time to spare and a complete, recognizable fish.", "my_share_percent": 35}
